newsitem.title: FRANCE: Promodes says is not in talks with Casino.
newsitem.headline: Promodes says is not in talks with Casino.

text.p: Retailer Promodes said on Thursday it was not holding any kind of merger discussions with supermarkets group Casino, refuting recurrent market rumours of a linkup.
"We formally deny any move toward Casino or any discussions. There are no talks under way," said Jacques Beauchet, director of communications at the company.
Speculation about a merger between the two companies has been rife since the takeover last year of Docks de France by privately-held Auchan.
Auchan's move was prompted by a new law in France that makes it harder for big retailers to expand floor space or set up new stores in an effort to protect small shops and city centres.

Interest in Casino and Promodes shares was heightened after Promodes chairman Paul-Louis Halley predicted the French food retailing industry would consolidate to around five groups. He also said in a newspaper interview that the Halley family envisaged reducing its stake in Promodes to below 30 percent.
Halley described the controlling shareholder of Casino, Jean-Charles Naouri, in very favourable terms in the interview.
Promodes subsequently rowed back, saying it was not in talks with Casino and that the company was large enough to ensure its development without an alliance, but the speculation continued.
The newspaper La Tribune on Thursday reported that market sources had calculated the terms of a share exchange at one share in Promodes for six in Casino.
Promodes shares were down 0.94 percent at 1,471 francs on the Paris bourse at 0905 GMT. Casino shares were up 1.79 percent at 250.50 francs in a slightly weaker market.
Promodes and Casino are ranked fifth and sixth, respectively, in France in terms of sales.
